### inspector-barbosa: pedantic inspection of reasoning-tool changes

**[Listed](#inspector-barbosa-rationale)**

Dev and pm inspection workflows for reasoning-tool changes, extrapolated from one developer's cvc5 commits and code reviews, with a cvc5 worked reference.

- **Source:** [skills/inspector-barbosa](<skills/inspector-barbosa>) (maintained in this repository)
- **License:** [MIT](<skills/inspector-barbosa/LICENSE.txt>)
- **Tags:** reasoning-tools, smt-solvers, sat-solvers, proof-checking, code-review, correctness, regression-testing, project-management
- **Last inspected:** 2026-10-22
- **Limitations:** Based on one developer on one project, not written by Haniel Barbosa (who agreed to the skill and its name) and not endorsed by the cvc5 project. Generalization beyond cvc5 is an extrapolation by the skill authors, not a cross-project evaluation. cvc5 details were checked at the recorded source revision and date; external checks are optional and skipped checks establish nothing.

<a id="inspector-barbosa-rationale"></a>**Why it is listed:** Helps maintainers and contributors of solvers, provers, and proof checkers review changes line by line and as pull requests. It separates blocking soundness and proof issues from nits, asks for documented contracts and minimized regressions, and keeps CI, follow-up issues, and release notes in order.

<a id="legendary-nbjorner-rationale"></a>**Why it is listed:** Helps developers of solvers, provers, model checkers, optimization and synthesis tools localize broken invariants, preserve models and witnesses, handle incomplete runs, and record regressions. Keeps the Z3 evidence separate from the authors' broader extrapolation and reports the limits of optional external checks.

**Evidence:**

- [usage-report](<https://github.com/ai4ardev/agent-skills/pull/15>) (positive): In a review and fix pass on a parity-game solver's benchmark runner, the skill's test-mode rules surfaced two problems that earlier reviews without it missed.   - Reported by: author

  - Context: strahler-tree-experiments (C23 parity-game solvers). Codex CLI with gpt-6.1-sol at xhigh effort, with the Ponytail skill; SKILL.md only, without references/z3.md. One review pass and one fix pass.
  - Limitations: One project and one review, reported by the skill's author. Not a controlled comparison; the earlier reviews without the skill covered different diffs. It shows the problems were found, not that the skill caused it.

<a id="oss-verify-add-project"></a>

### OSS Verify add-project: fuzz targets as formal specifications

**[Listed](#oss-verify-add-project-rationale)**

Guides an agent and a project maintainer through enrolling a C, C++, Rust, Python, or Go project in OSS Verify, which proves theorems about the project's fuzz targets.

- **Source:** [https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-project/SKILL.md](<https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-project/SKILL.md>) (revision ab988414395c38b448bbc78125c103248b5c7aa4)
- **License:** [Apache-2.0](<https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify/blob/main/LICENSE>)
- **Tags:** formal-verification, specification, fuzzing, correctness
- **Last inspected:** 2026-10-23
- **Limitations:** Written for enrollment in the OSS Verify service operated by Theorem Labs and meant to run inside the theorem-labs/oss-verify repository; the steps reference its documents, templates, and tools. Its tools/check script builds the project's Dockerfile with network access, and findings and patches from the service are generated by AI models. Listed as examined at the recorded revision; not reviewed or tested by this catalog.

<a id="oss-verify-add-project-rationale"></a>**Why it is listed:** Teaches how to write a fuzz target that states what "correct" means so that a proof about it is not vacuous. Each property becomes a check that aborts, never assert(), which NDEBUG removes. A coverage witness shows each check runs, and a distinguishing mutant shows each property can fail. Inputs and decoding are total, bounded, and deterministic, and the agent asks the maintainer rather than guessing. These practices carry over to specifying any library for verification or property-based testing.
